brief: At the beginning of the fourth century, the Roman emperors clamped down on recent innovations in the empire such as Christianity, and began systematic persecution of the church. Among those killed was Lucy of Syracuse in Sicily. We know nothing else about her, but her cult became widespread. Later stories described her as a wealthy virgin who gave help to the poor and was betrayed by an irate suitor. She died in 304. The derivation of her name from the Latin word for light makes light an appropriate theme for Lucy.
